units.passage: Grammarly’s Generative AI Tools and Copilot Students are responsible for following course- and/or assignment-specific AI policies. If a professor has not permitted the use of AI tools, then using the generative AI function in Grammarly or CoPilot to create part of a draft may violate the Honor Code. If the professor allows the use of these tools, or others like them, please make sure you follow any disclosure requirements (e.g., citation, addendum, etc.). Grammarly Writing Support vs. Generative AI Tools Grammarly has two sets of tools. If you plan to use Grammarly and your professor has banned the use of AI tools, please make sure you have turned the generative AI function off . For more information, please see Grammarly’s Introducing generative AI assistance . Grammarly’s core grammar and revision tools (spelling, clarity, fluency, tone) are reactive. They provide in-line suggestions based on what a student has already written, helping improve what’s there, but not writing it for them. These tools are typically viewed as learning aids . Grammarly’s generative AI , by contrast, can be used to generate or rephrase content using prompts.

units.passage: A type of AI that has the ability to understand, learn, and apply knowledge in a way that is indistinguishable from human intelligence. AGI can perform any intellectual task that a human can do. Supervised Learning : A type of machine learning where the model is trained on labeled data, meaning the input data is paired with the correct output. The model learns to make predictions based on this training data. Unsupervised Learning : A type of machine learning where the model is trained on unlabeled data and must find patterns and relationships in the data without any guidance on what the output should be. Reinforcement Learning : A type of machine learning where an agent learns to make decisions by taking actions in an environment to maximize some notion of cumulative reward. Computer Vision : A field of AI that enables computers to interpret and make decisions based on visual data from the world, such as images and videos. Robotics : The branch of technology that deals with the design, construction, operation, and application of robots, often incorporating AI to enable autonomous behavior. Generative AI : A type of AI that can create new content, such as text, images, or music, based on the data it has been trained on.
units.why: Defines generative AI ("create new content, such as text, images, or music"), setting what the policy covers; P61.

units.why: 'Generative AI encompasses models and systems designed to produce novel content, such as text, images, audio, or code' defines the tool class that most course policies target. P61 fits.

units.passage: AI agents are systems that perceive their environment, make decisions, and take actions to achieve specific goals.
units.why: 'AI agents are systems that perceive their environment, make decisions, and take actions to achieve specific goals' defines agents, so the site's scope includes autonomous systems. P61 fits.

units.passage: Some AI tools make suggestions
units.why: 'Some AI tools make suggestions (such as Word's grammar checker) and may seem so familiar that we don't even think of them as AI' distinguishes suggestive from generative tools. P61 fits because it sets what counts as AI.
units.fit_note: Coder B (P100): Does not exempt them from rules; only notes they are familiar and suggestive.

units.passage: Any system, software, hardware, application, tool, or utility that operates in whole or in part using AI.
units.why: Defines "AI System" as any system or tool that operates in whole or in part using AI; a definition setting scope, P61.

units.passage: In short, Generative AI refers to deep-learning models that can generate outputs based on data that they are trained on.
units.why: Defines generative AI as "deep-learning models that can generate outputs based on data that they are trained on"; a definition, P61.

units.passage: Generative AI includes both standalone offerings such as ChatGPT, and offerings that are embedded in other software, such as Github Copilot
units.why: The Generative AI definition ends "Generative AI includes both standalone offerings such as ChatGPT, and offerings that are embedded in other software, such as Github Copilot", which fixes what the guidelines cover. It is scope, so P61, informs; the Copilot mention does not add a rule about editors.
units.fit_note: Only names embedded tools like Copilot as within scope; sets no rule about using or disabling them. / Also says generative AI embedded in other software such as Github Copilot is covered, touching P07.

units.passage: Generative Artificial Intelligence (Generative AI or GenAI) refers to systems that can create new content, such as text, images, music, or other digital content in response to prompts provided by its user.
units.why: The page defines "Generative Artificial Intelligence ... refers to systems that can create new content", which sets what the policy covers, so P61.

units.passage: Generative AI describes an array of technologies that are capable of creating new text, images, code, audio, video, or other content.
units.policy: Generative AI describes an array of technologies that are capable of creating new text, images, code, audio, video, or other content
units.why: The definition 'Generative AI describes an array of technologies that are capable of creating new text, images, code, audio, video' sets what the guidance covers (P61).
